-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE OPS1: CORPORATE PAYMENTS 360 AGENT   (~45 min)
-- Persona: Payments Operations analyst (no SQL needed after setup)
-- Question: "Before I call a client, tell me everything: payments health,
--            open incidents, and what they have been complaining about."
-- Prereq:   setup/catchup/core_analytics.sql + DA1 (SV_CLIENT_360)
--           + setup/catchup/semantic_view_and_agent.sql (SV_PAYMENTS)
--           Facilitator shortcut: run all three catch-up/DA1 scripts in order.
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- OPS1.1 The agent: two semantic views as tools + charting
-- Created in SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE.AGENTS so it appears in Snowflake CoWork
-- for everyone with access.
-- (Snowsight alternative: AI & ML > Agents > Create agent - same settings.)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE AGENT SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE.AGENTS.CORPORATE_PAYMENTS_360
  COMMENT = 'Barclays HOL - Corporate Payments 360: client payments health, incidents and sentiment'
  PROFILE = '{"display_name": "Corporate Payments 360", "color": "blue"}'
  FROM SPECIFICATION
  $$
  models:
    orchestration: auto

  orchestration:
    budget:
      seconds: 90
      tokens: 20000

  instructions:
    response: >
      You support Payments Operations and Relationship Managers in a UK corporate bank.
      Lead with a one-line summary, then the supporting numbers.
      Format money in GBP with thousands separators and percentages to 1 decimal place.
      When briefing on a client, always cover: payment volume and success rate,
      failed value, open and critical alerts, and feedback sentiment with the main topic.
      If the data cannot answer the question, say so - never guess.
    orchestration: >
      Use Client360 for anything about a specific client, relationship manager,
      KYC status, alerts or incidents, and client feedback.
      Use PaymentsOps for scheme-level and daily trends: volumes by scheme/region/channel,
      processing times, P95 latency and SLA compliance or breaches.
      For a client briefing you may need Client360 more than once.
    sample_questions:
      - question: "Brief me on the client with the most failed payment value"
      - question: "Which relationship managers have the most open critical alerts?"
      - question: "Which payment schemes breached SLA most often in the last 30 days?"
      - question: "Show weekly payment volume for CHAPS as a chart"

  tools:
    - tool_spec:
        type: cortex_analyst_text_to_sql
        name: Client360
        description: >
          Corporate client 360: one row per client with sector, country, KYC status and RM;
          payment totals, success rate and failed value per client; AI-scored feedback
          sentiment and topic; and operational alerts with severity, status and resolution time.
    - tool_spec:
        type: cortex_analyst_text_to_sql
        name: PaymentsOps
        description: >
          Daily payment KPIs by scheme (CHAPS, Faster Payments, BACS, SWIFT, SEPA, Wire),
          region, channel, sector and RM, plus daily SLA compliance status per scheme.
    - tool_spec:
        type: data_to_chart
        name: data_to_chart
        description: Generates charts from query results

  tool_resources:
    Client360:
      semantic_view: BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.SV_CLIENT_360
      execution_environment:
        type: warehouse
        warehouse: BARCLAYS_WH
    PaymentsOps:
      semantic_view: BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.SV_PAYMENTS
      execution_environment:
        type: warehouse
        warehouse: BARCLAYS_WH
  $$;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- OPS1.2 Use it - Snowflake CoWork (formerly Snowflake Intelligence)
-- Select "Corporate Payments 360" and try:
--   1. "Brief me on the client with the most failed payment value"
--   2. "Which of Priya Sharma's clients have open critical alerts?"
--   3. "Is SWIFT meeting its SLA this month? Show a chart."
--   4. "Which clients have negative sentiment AND a success rate below 96%?"
-- Expand "Show details" on each answer to see the tool and SQL used.
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- OPS1.3 The same agent from SQL (e.g. embedding in a process or app)
SELECT SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.DATA_AGENT_RUN(
  'SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE.AGENTS.CORPORATE_PAYMENTS_360',
  $${"messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Which relationship managers have the most open critical alerts?"}]}]}$$
) AS RESPONSE;

-- sees what their role is granted (see GOV1 for masking and row access).

modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE OPS2: ALERT TRIAGE + NEGATIVE SENTIMENT FEED   (~30 min)
-- Persona: Payments Operations analyst / team lead
-- Question: "Which open alerts should my team work first, what should we do,
--            and which unhappy clients are linked to them?"
-- Prereq:   setup/catchup/core_analytics.sql (FEEDBACK_ENRICHED, STG_* views)
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;
USE SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- OPS2.1 Live negative-sentiment feed for the CX escalation queue
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE DYNAMIC TABLE DT_NEGATIVE_SENTIMENT_FEED
    TARGET_LAG = '5 minutes'
    WAREHOUSE  = BARCLAYS_WH
AS
SELECT FEEDBACK_ID, FEEDBACK_DATE, CUSTOMER_ID, CUSTOMER_NAME, CUSTOMER_SECTOR,
       RM_NAME, PAYMENT_ID, PAYMENT_TYPE, FEEDBACK_TEXT, SENTIMENT_SCORE, TOPIC_CATEGORY
FROM FEEDBACK_ENRICHED
WHERE SENTIMENT_LABEL = 'NEGATIVE';

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- OPS2.2 Prioritised triage queue: open alerts, scored for urgency
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW V_ALERT_TRIAGE_QUEUE AS
SELECT al.ALERT_ID, al.ALERT_TIME, al.SEVERITY, al.STATUS, al.ASSIGNED_TO,
       al.PAYMENT_TYPE, al.ALERT_DESCRIPTION,
       p.PAYMENT_ID, p.AMOUNT, p.CURRENCY, p.STATUS AS PAYMENT_STATUS,
       e.ERROR_CODE, e.ERROR_DESCRIPTION, e.ERROR_CATEGORY, e.IS_RETRYABLE,
       c.CUSTOMER_NAME, c.RM_NAME,
       COUNT(n.FEEDBACK_ID) AS CLIENT_NEGATIVE_FEEDBACK,
       -- simple, explainable priority score
       DECODE(al.SEVERITY, 'CRITICAL', 40, 'HIGH', 25, 'MEDIUM', 10, 0)
         + IFF(p.AMOUNT >= 1000000, 30, IFF(p.AMOUNT >= 100000, 15, 0))
         + LEAST(COUNT(n.FEEDBACK_ID), 20)
         + IFF(e.ERROR_CATEGORY = 'COMPLIANCE', 10, 0)        AS PRIORITY_SCORE
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.OPERATIONAL_ALERTS al
JOIN STG_PAYMENTS p          ON al.PAYMENT_ID = p.PAYMENT_ID
LEFT JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.ERROR_CODES e ON p.ERROR_CODE = e.ERROR_CODE
LEFT JOIN STG_ACCOUNTS a     ON p.ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID
LEFT JOIN STG_CUSTOMERS c    ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
LEFT JOIN DT_NEGATIVE_SENTIMENT_FEED n ON n.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
WHERE al.STATUS <> 'RESOLVED'
GROUP BY ALL;

SELECT ALERT_ID, SEVERITY, PAYMENT_TYPE, AMOUNT, ERROR_DESCRIPTION, CUSTOMER_NAME,
       CLIENT_NEGATIVE_FEEDBACK, PRIORITY_SCORE
FROM V_ALERT_TRIAGE_QUEUE
ORDER BY PRIORITY_SCORE DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- OPS2.3 AI-recommended next action for the top of the queue
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ALERT_RECOMMENDATIONS AS
SELECT ALERT_ID, SEVERITY, PAYMENT_TYPE, CUSTOMER_NAME, RM_NAME, PRIORITY_SCORE,
       AI_COMPLETE('claude-sonnet-4-5',
         'You are a senior payments operations analyst at a UK bank. In at most 3 short bullet points, '
         || 'give the next actions for this alert, including whether to retry the payment and whether to contact the client or their RM. '
         || 'Alert: ' || ALERT_DESCRIPTION
         || ' | Scheme: ' || PAYMENT_TYPE
         || ' | Error: ' || COALESCE(ERROR_DESCRIPTION, 'none') || ' (' || COALESCE(ERROR_CATEGORY, 'n/a')
         || ', retryable=' || COALESCE(IS_RETRYABLE::STRING, 'unknown') || ')'
         || ' | Amount: ' || AMOUNT || ' ' || CURRENCY
         || ' | Client negative feedback items: ' || CLIENT_NEGATIVE_FEEDBACK) AS RECOMMENDED_ACTION
FROM V_ALERT_TRIAGE_QUEUE
ORDER BY PRIORITY_SCORE DESC
LIMIT 10;

SELECT ALERT_ID, SEVERITY, CUSTOMER_NAME, RECOMMENDED_ACTION
FROM ALERT_RECOMMENDATIONS ORDER BY PRIORITY_SCORE DESC;

-- =====================================================
-- OPS3: Payments operations in Snowflake CoWork - reference SQL
-- OPS3 is done in the CoWork UI and a Workspace dashboard; this is the SQL behind it.
-- The agent and semantic view are built at provisioning (setup/09_cowork_pack.sql).
-- =====================================================
USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;

-- 1. The agent CoWork lists, and its tools (Analyst + code execution)
SHOW AGENTS IN SCHEMA SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE.AGENTS;
DESCRIBE AGENT SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE.AGENTS.PAYMENTS_OPS_COWORK;

-- 2. The semantic view it answers from
SHOW SEMANTIC METRICS IN BARCLAYS_HOL.COWORK_PACK.SV_PAYMENTS_OPS;

-- 3. The same numbers as the chart step: monthly failed value by scheme, last 12 months
SELECT * FROM SEMANTIC_VIEW(
    BARCLAYS_HOL.COWORK_PACK.SV_PAYMENTS_OPS
    DIMENSIONS payments.payment_month, payments.payment_type
    METRICS payments.failed_value
    WHERE payments.payment_month >= DATEADD('month', -12, DATE_TRUNC('month', CURRENT_DATE()))
)
ORDER BY PAYMENT_MONTH, PAYMENT_TYPE;

-- 4. The Logistics story behind the Deep Research step: feedback that mentions leaving, by sector,
--    and the sector's payment failure rate (which isn't unusual - the issue is service, not failures)
WITH feedback AS (
    SELECT CUSTOMER_SECTOR,
           COUNT_IF(FEEDBACK_MONTH >= DATEADD('month', -4, DATE_TRUNC('month', CURRENT_DATE()))) AS RECENT_FEEDBACK,
           COUNT_IF(FEEDBACK_TEXT ILIKE ANY ('%other banking providers%', '%another bank%', '%tender%')) AS CHURN_MENTIONS
    FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.COWORK_PACK.CLIENT_FEEDBACK
    GROUP BY 1
), payments AS (
    SELECT CUSTOMER_SECTOR, ROUND(COUNT_IF(STATUS = 'FAILED') / COUNT(*) * 100, 1) AS FAILURE_RATE_PCT
    FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.COWORK_PACK.PAYMENT_ACTIVITY
    WHERE PAYMENT_DATE >= DATEADD('month', -4, CURRENT_DATE())
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT f.CUSTOMER_SECTOR, f.RECENT_FEEDBACK, f.CHURN_MENTIONS, p.FAILURE_RATE_PCT
FROM feedback f LEFT JOIN payments p USING (CUSTOMER_SECTOR)
ORDER BY f.CHURN_MENTIONS DESC, f.CUSTOMER_SECTOR;

-- 5. The automation step's question: top 5 clients by failed value last week
SELECT CUSTOMER_NAME, RM_NAME, PAYMENT_TYPE AS MAIN_FAILING_SCHEME, FAILED_VALUE
FROM (
    SELECT CUSTOMER_NAME, RM_NAME, PAYMENT_TYPE, SUM(AMOUNT) AS FAILED_VALUE,
           SUM(SUM(AMOUNT)) OVER (PARTITION BY CUSTOMER_NAME) AS CLIENT_FAILED_VALUE,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CUSTOMER_NAME ORDER BY SUM(AMOUNT) DESC) AS RN
    FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.COWORK_PACK.PAYMENT_ACTIVITY
    WHERE STATUS = 'FAILED'
      AND PAYMENT_DATE >= DATEADD('week', -1, DATE_TRUNC('week', CURRENT_DATE()))
      AND PAYMENT_DATE <  DATE_TRUNC('week', CURRENT_DATE())
    GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
)
WHERE RN = 1
ORDER BY CLIENT_FAILED_VALUE DESC
LIMIT 5;

-- 6. Dashboard tile queries (what Cortex Code should generate for payments_ops)
--    Scorecards
SELECT SUM(AMOUNT) AS PAYMENT_VALUE,
       ROUND(COUNT_IF(STATUS = 'COMPLETED') / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) * 100, 1) AS SUCCESS_RATE_PCT,
       SUM(IFF(STATUS = 'FAILED', AMOUNT, 0)) AS FAILED_VALUE
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.COWORK_PACK.PAYMENT_ACTIVITY
WHERE PAYMENT_DATE >= DATEADD('month', -12, CURRENT_DATE());
--    Top 10 clients by failed value
SELECT CUSTOMER_NAME, CUSTOMER_SECTOR, RM_NAME, SUM(AMOUNT) AS FAILED_VALUE, COUNT(*) AS FAILED_PAYMENTS
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.COWORK_PACK.PAYMENT_ACTIVITY
WHERE STATUS = 'FAILED' AND PAYMENT_DATE >= DATEADD('month', -12, CURRENT_DATE())
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY FAILED_VALUE DESC
LIMIT 10;
--    Failed payments by error code
SELECT ERROR_CODE, COUNT(*) AS FAILED_PAYMENTS, SUM(AMOUNT) AS FAILED_VALUE
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.COWORK_PACK.PAYMENT_ACTIVITY
WHERE STATUS = 'FAILED' AND PAYMENT_DATE >= DATEADD('month', -12, CURRENT_DATE())
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY FAILED_PAYMENTS DESC;

modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE AI1: AGENT WITH CUSTOM TOOLS   (~45 min)
-- Persona: AI Builder
-- Question: "Ops staff ask about specific payments by ID and about scheme
--            rules - not just aggregates. Give the agent precise tools."
-- Prereq:   setup/catchup/core_analytics.sql + setup/catchup/semantic_view_and_agent.sql
-- Builds:   2 UDF tools + PAYMENTS_INVESTIGATOR agent
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;
USE SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.AGENTS;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- AI1.1 Tool 1: exact payment lookup (deterministic - no text-to-SQL guessing)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION GET_PAYMENT_DETAILS(PAYMENT_ID_IN VARCHAR)
RETURNS TABLE (PAYMENT_ID VARCHAR, PAYMENT_DATE TIMESTAMP, PAYMENT_TYPE VARCHAR,
               AMOUNT NUMBER(15,2), CURRENCY VARCHAR, STATUS VARCHAR,
               PROCESSING_TIME_MS NUMBER, ERROR_CODE VARCHAR, ERROR_DESCRIPTION VARCHAR,
               IS_RETRYABLE BOOLEAN, CUSTOMER_NAME VARCHAR, RM_NAME VARCHAR,
               OPEN_ALERTS NUMBER)
COMMENT = 'Look up one payment by PAYMENT_ID with its error, client, RM and open alert count'
AS
$$
    SELECT p.PAYMENT_ID, p.PAYMENT_DATE, p.PAYMENT_TYPE, p.AMOUNT, p.CURRENCY, p.STATUS,
           p.PROCESSING_TIME_MS, p.ERROR_CODE, e.ERROR_DESCRIPTION, e.IS_RETRYABLE,
           c.CUSTOMER_NAME, c.RM_NAME,
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.OPERATIONAL_ALERTS al
             WHERE al.PAYMENT_ID = p.PAYMENT_ID AND al.STATUS <> 'RESOLVED')
    FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_PAYMENTS p
    LEFT JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.ERROR_CODES e  ON p.ERROR_CODE = e.ERROR_CODE
    LEFT JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_ACCOUNTS a ON p.ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID
    LEFT JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_CUSTOMERS c ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
    WHERE p.PAYMENT_ID = UPPER(TRIM(PAYMENT_ID_IN))
$$;

-- Agent custom tools need a scalar return - wrap the table function as JSON
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION PAYMENT_LOOKUP(PAYMENT_ID VARCHAR)
RETURNS VARIANT
COMMENT = 'Agent tool: payment details as JSON'
AS
$$
    SELECT COALESCE(ARRAY_AGG(OBJECT_CONSTRUCT(*))[0],
                    OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('error', 'No payment found with ID ' || PAYMENT_ID))
    FROM TABLE(GET_PAYMENT_DETAILS(PAYMENT_ID))
$$;

SELECT PAYMENT_LOOKUP((SELECT MIN(PAYMENT_ID) FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS WHERE STATUS = 'FAILED')) AS RESULT;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- AI1.2 Tool 2: scheme rules ("can I still send this today?")
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION SCHEME_RULES(SCHEME VARCHAR)
RETURNS VARIANT
COMMENT = 'Agent tool: payment scheme rules - settlement cycle, value limit, cutoff and SLA'
AS
$$
    SELECT COALESCE(ARRAY_AGG(OBJECT_CONSTRUCT(
               'scheme', s.SCHEME_CODE, 'name', s.SCHEME_NAME,
               'settlement_cycle', s.SETTLEMENT_CYCLE, 'domestic', s.IS_DOMESTIC,
               'max_value_gbp', s.MAX_VALUE_GBP, 'cutoff_time_uk', s.CUTOFF_TIME::STRING,
               'currency', s.OPERATING_CURRENCY,
               'sla_target_success_rate', sla.TARGET_SUCCESS_RATE,
               'sla_max_p95_ms', sla.MAX_PROCESSING_TIME_MS))[0],
             OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('error', 'Unknown scheme. Valid: CHAPS, FASTER_PAYMENTS, BACS, SWIFT, SEPA, WIRE_TRANSFER'))
    FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENT_SCHEMES s
    LEFT JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.SLA_DEFINITIONS sla ON sla.PAYMENT_TYPE = s.SCHEME_CODE
    WHERE s.SCHEME_CODE = UPPER(REPLACE(TRIM(SCHEME), ' ', '_'))
$$;

SELECT SCHEME_RULES('chaps') AS RESULT;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- AI1.3 The agent: Analyst for aggregates + custom tools for precision
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE AGENT BARCLAYS_HOL.AGENTS.PAYMENTS_INVESTIGATOR
  COMMENT = 'Barclays HOL - investigates individual payments and scheme rules, plus KPI questions'
  PROFILE = '{"display_name": "Payments Investigator", "color": "green"}'
  FROM SPECIFICATION
  $$
  models:
    orchestration: auto
  instructions:
    response: >
      You help payments operations investigate individual payments. Be precise and brief.
      When reporting a payment, state status, error and whether it is retryable first.
    orchestration: >
      If the user gives a payment ID (format PAY followed by digits), call PaymentLookup.
      For questions about a scheme's cutoff, limit, settlement cycle or SLA, call SchemeRules.
      For counts, volumes, trends or comparisons, use PaymentsOps.
      You can chain tools, e.g. look up a payment then check its scheme's cutoff.
  tools:
    - tool_spec:
        type: generic
        name: PaymentLookup
        description: Returns full details for a single payment ID, including error, retryability, client, RM and open alerts.
        input_schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            payment_id:
              type: string
              description: The payment ID, e.g. PAY0000000123
          required: [payment_id]
    - tool_spec:
        type: generic
        name: SchemeRules
        description: Returns rules for a payment scheme - settlement cycle, max value, daily cutoff time and SLA targets.
        input_schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            scheme:
              type: string
              description: One of CHAPS, FASTER_PAYMENTS, BACS, SWIFT, SEPA, WIRE_TRANSFER
          required: [scheme]
    - tool_spec:
        type: cortex_analyst_text_to_sql
        name: PaymentsOps
        description: Aggregated daily payment KPIs and SLA compliance by scheme, region, channel, sector and RM.
  tool_resources:
    PaymentLookup:
      type: function
      identifier: BARCLAYS_HOL.AGENTS.PAYMENT_LOOKUP
      execution_environment:
        type: warehouse
        warehouse: BARCLAYS_WH
    SchemeRules:
      type: function
      identifier: BARCLAYS_HOL.AGENTS.SCHEME_RULES
      execution_environment:
        type: warehouse
        warehouse: BARCLAYS_WH
    PaymentsOps:
      semantic_view: BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.SV_PAYMENTS
      execution_environment:
        type: warehouse
        warehouse: BARCLAYS_WH
  $$;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- AI1.4 Test (Snowsight: AI & ML > Agents > PAYMENTS_INVESTIGATOR > Playground)
-- Grab a failed payment ID to ask about:
SELECT PAYMENT_ID, PAYMENT_TYPE, AMOUNT FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS WHERE STATUS = 'FAILED' LIMIT 3;
-- Try:
--   "What happened to payment <ID>? Can we retry it, and is there still time before the scheme cutoff today?"
--   "What's the maximum value for Faster Payments, and how many failed last week?"
-- CoCo prompt: "Add a third tool to PAYMENTS_INVESTIGATOR that lists the open alerts
--   for a given customer name, using a new UDF in BARCLAYS_HOL.AGENTS."
-- -----------------------------------------------------

SELECT 'AI1 complete' AS STATUS;

-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE AI2: SNOWFLAKE-MANAGED MCP SERVER   (~30 min)
-- Persona: AI Builder
-- Question: "Our teams use different AI clients (Cortex Code, Claude, Copilot,
--            in-house apps). Expose governed payments tools to all of them once."

--           and the Marketplace knowledge extension installed by facilitator setup.

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;

modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE AI3: MARKETPLACE KNOWLEDGE EXTENSION (instead of Cortex Search)   (~30 min)
-- Persona: AI Builder
-- Question: "Our agents need trusted unstructured knowledge, but we are not
--            allowed to vectorise internal (PII) data yet. What can we do?"
-- Prereq:   Facilitator setup 00 (installs SNOWFLAKE_DOCS_CKE), DA1 (SV_CLIENT_360)
--
-- A Cortex Knowledge Extension (CKE) is a search service that a Marketplace
-- provider builds, hosts and refreshes. You query it through a share - no
-- internal data is embedded, indexed or sent to the provider.
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- AI3.1 What did we get from the Marketplace?
-- Snowsight: Data Products > Marketplace > search "Cortex Knowledge Extension"
-- (Finance publishers such as Investopedia are listed; personalised listings
--  must be requested by the account admin.)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SHOW CORTEX SEARCH SERVICES IN DATABASE SNOWFLAKE_DOCS_CKE;
-- Note: we did not create this service, we cannot see its source table,
-- and we pay only for the queries we run.

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- AI3.2 Query it directly
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT r.value:DOCUMENT_TITLE::STRING AS TITLE,
       r.value:SOURCE_URL::STRING     AS URL,
       LEFT(r.value:CHUNK::STRING, 200) AS EXCERPT
FROM TABLE(FLATTEN(PARSE_JSON(SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SEARCH_PREVIEW(
        'SNOWFLAKE_DOCS_CKE.SHARED.CKE_SNOWFLAKE_DOCS_SERVICE',
        '{"query": "How do I apply a masking policy to a column?",
          "columns": ["DOCUMENT_TITLE", "SOURCE_URL", "CHUNK"],
          "limit": 3}')):results)) r;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- AI3.3 Combine governed internal data + external knowledge in one agent
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE AGENT SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE.AGENTS.PAYMENTS_PLATFORM_COPILOT
  COMMENT = 'Barclays HOL - client data (semantic view) + Snowflake docs (Marketplace knowledge extension)'
  PROFILE = '{"display_name": "Payments Platform Copilot", "color": "orange"}'
  FROM SPECIFICATION
  $$
  models:
    orchestration: auto
  instructions:
    response: >
      Be concise. When you use documentation, cite the source URL.
      Never present documentation content as if it were bank data.
    orchestration: >
      Use Client360 for any question about our clients, payments, alerts or feedback.
      Use PlatformDocs for how-to questions about Snowflake features
      (Iceberg, dynamic tables, policies, semantic views, agents).
      A question may need both, e.g. "which clients have X, and how do I monitor that?"
  tools:
    - tool_spec:
        type: cortex_analyst_text_to_sql
        name: Client360
        description: Corporate client payments health, alerts and feedback sentiment.
    - tool_spec:
        type: cortex_search
        name: PlatformDocs
        description: Official Snowflake documentation from a Marketplace Cortex Knowledge Extension.
  tool_resources:
    Client360:
      semantic_view: BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.SV_CLIENT_360
      execution_environment:
        type: warehouse
        warehouse: BARCLAYS_WH
    PlatformDocs:
      name: SNOWFLAKE_DOCS_CKE.SHARED.CKE_SNOWFLAKE_DOCS_SERVICE
      max_results: 4
      title_column: DOCUMENT_TITLE
      id_column: SOURCE_URL
  $$;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- AI3.4 Try it in Snowflake CoWork ("Payments Platform Copilot"):
--   "Which 3 clients have the most open critical alerts, and how could I build
--    a dynamic table that keeps that list up to date?"
--   "How do Snowflake-managed Iceberg tables differ from ones using an external volume?"
-- Or from SQL:
SELECT SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.DATA_AGENT_RUN(
  'SNOWFLAKE_INTELLIGENCE.AGENTS.PAYMENTS_PLATFORM_COPILOT',
  $${"messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Which 3 clients have the most open critical alerts, and how could I build a dynamic table to keep that list up to date?"}]}]}$$
) AS RESPONSE;
-- -----------------------------------------------------

-- Discussion: the same pattern works for licensed external content already
-- used by the investment bank (LSEG, FactSet, S&P - several publish CKEs),
-- giving retail and corporate banking AI over trusted text with no PII risk.

SELECT 'AI3 complete' AS STATUS;

steps.body: **Tip:** the people and the text are synthetic, written to match each customer's records: leavers call before they leave, fraud victims call about their own fraud.

steps.prompt: Create the table BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.RB_CALL_INSIGHTS from the 300 most recent calls in RB_CALL_TRANSCRIPTS (since 1 Aug 2026), with AI_SENTIMENT's overall sentiment, a CALL_REASON from AI_CLASSIFY (savings rates, branch access, service complaint, fraud or scam, financial difficulty, card or app problem, product question, account admin), and VULNERABILITY_CUES from AI_CLASSIFY in multi-label mode (mentions health or disability, bereavement, money worries, none). steps.expect: about 300 enriched calls. Service complaints and savings-rate calls are the most negative, and those callers are the most likely to have left.

steps.expect: one row per complaint with product, amount and requested outcome filled in from the free text

steps.expect: one summary naming reasons such as low savings rates, branch closures, unresolved complaints and switching offers, each with an action

Then for 3 phishing screenshots, use AI_COMPLETE with the image to say which organisation the message impersonates and list its red flags.
steps.expect: crime references starting NFRC, amounts that match the case losses, and screenshots identified as fake parcel-delivery, HMRC refund or bank "new payee" messages, each with red flags such as a lookalike web address

steps.title: Draft a fraud case decision
steps.body: **Important:** AI drafts, people decide. The investigator still owns the reimbursement decision.
steps.prompt: For one APP scam case in RB_FRAUD_CASES, combine the investigator notes, the customer's fraud call transcript (RB_CALL_TRANSCRIPTS in the FRAUD queue with the same TXN_ID as the case's FIRST_FRAUD_TXN_ID), the customer's VULNERABLE_FLAG and age from RB_CUSTOMERS, and the recorded DECISION. Use AI_COMPLETE to draft a 150-word case summary with a reimbursement recommendation that cites the evidence, and flag anything in the sources that disagrees.
steps.expect: a decision draft that quotes the case's amounts and dates and agrees with the recorded decision, or flags where the sources disagree

steps.title: Check SAR narrative quality
steps.body:
**Tip:** QA_ISSUE is the answer key: the gap each narrative was written with. In real life you wouldn't have one, so a check like this is a first pass before a person reviews the SAR.
**Tip:** Asking AI_EXTRACT one question per element works better than asking AI_CLASSIFY to judge "complete or not": classifiers lean towards "complete" when something is simply absent.
steps.prompt: Check every narrative in RB_SAR_NARRATIVES against a simple standard. Use AI_EXTRACT with four questions: why the bank considers the activity suspicious, the specific date, the specific amount in pounds, and the action the bank took, each answering None if the narrative doesn't say. Turn the answers into one finding per SAR (COMPLETE, MISSING_REASON, MISSING_DATES_AMOUNTS or MISSING_ACTION), then compare it with the QA_ISSUE column in a confusion table and show the share that match.
steps.expect: about 80 to 85% match. Every complete SAR passes, and missing dates, amounts and actions are caught; a missing reason is the hardest, because the model infers one from the activity

modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- AI4: AI SQL ON CALL TRANSCRIPTS, COMPLAINTS AND FINANCIAL CRIME EVIDENCE - reference SQL
-- Approved AI SQL functions only (AI_SENTIMENT, AI_CLASSIFY, AI_EXTRACT, AI_AGG, AI_COMPLETE).
-- Run as HOL_PARTICIPANT. Samples keep the AI credits small; drop the LIMITs to do the lot.
-- =====================================================
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;
USE SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS;

-- 1. Enrich call transcripts once: sentiment, reason and vulnerability cues
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE RB_CALL_INSIGHTS AS
SELECT t.CALL_ID, t.CUSTOMER_ID, t.CALL_START_TS, t.QUEUE, t.TOPIC,
       AI_SENTIMENT(t.TRANSCRIPT):categories[0]:sentiment::VARCHAR AS SENTIMENT,
       AI_CLASSIFY(t.TRANSCRIPT, ['savings rates', 'branch access', 'service complaint', 'fraud or scam',
                                 'financial difficulty', 'card or app problem', 'product question', 'account admin']):labels[0]::VARCHAR AS CALL_REASON,
       AI_CLASSIFY(t.TRANSCRIPT, ['mentions health or disability', 'mentions bereavement', 'mentions money worries', 'none'],
                   {'output_mode': 'multi'}):labels AS VULNERABILITY_CUES,
       c.CHURNED, c.AFFORDABILITY_BAND
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_CALL_TRANSCRIPTS t
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_CUSTOMERS c ON c.CUSTOMER_ID = t.CUSTOMER_ID
WHERE t.CALL_START_TS >= '2026-08-01'
LIMIT 300;

-- Does call sentiment line up with who left?
SELECT CALL_REASON, COUNT(*) AS CALLS, ROUND(100 * AVG(IFF(SENTIMENT = 'negative', 1, 0))) AS PCT_NEGATIVE,
       ROUND(100 * AVG(IFF(CHURNED, 1, 0))) AS PCT_CALLERS_WHO_LEFT
FROM RB_CALL_INSIGHTS GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY CALLS DESC;

-- 2. Pull structured fields out of complaints
SELECT COMPLAINT_ID, CATEGORY,
       AI_EXTRACT(text => COMPLAINT_TEXT, responseFormat => {
           'product': 'Which bank product is the complaint about?',
           'amount_gbp': 'What amount of money in pounds is mentioned, as a number?',
           'requested_outcome': 'What does the customer want the bank to do?'}):response AS EXTRACTED
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_COMPLAINTS
LIMIT 10;

-- 3. What leavers said in the 3 months before leaving, in one paragraph
SELECT AI_AGG(t.TRANSCRIPT, 'These calls are from retail bank customers who closed their accounts soon after. List the top 5 reasons they gave, with how often each came up, and one action the bank could take for each.') AS WHY_THEY_LEFT
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_CALL_TRANSCRIPTS t
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_CUSTOMERS c ON c.CUSTOMER_ID = t.CUSTOMER_ID
WHERE c.CHURNED AND t.CALL_START_TS BETWEEN DATEADD(month, -3, c.CHURN_DATE) AND c.CHURN_DATE;

-- 4. Police report PDFs: extract the crime reference and loss, and reconcile to the case
SELECT e.CASE_ID, f.LOSS_GBP AS CASE_LOSS_GBP,
       AI_EXTRACT(file => TO_FILE('@BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.FINCRIME_EVIDENCE', e.FILE_NAME), responseFormat => {
           'crime_reference': 'What is the crime reference number?',
           'date_reported': 'What date was it reported?',
           'amount_lost': 'What amount was lost, as a number?'}):response AS FROM_PDF
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_EVIDENCE_FILES e
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_FRAUD_CASES f ON f.CASE_ID = e.CASE_ID
WHERE e.EVIDENCE_TYPE = 'POLICE_REPORT_PDF'
LIMIT 5;

-- 5. Phishing screenshots: who is being impersonated, and the red flags
SELECT e.CASE_ID, e.FILE_NAME,
       AI_COMPLETE('claude-sonnet-4-5',
                   'This is a screenshot a fraud victim sent to their bank. Which organisation does the message impersonate, and what are its red flags? Answer in two short lines.',
                   TO_FILE('@BARCLAYS_HOL.RETAIL.FINCRIME_EVIDENCE', e.FILE_NAME)) AS ANALYSIS
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_EVIDENCE_FILES e
WHERE e.EVIDENCE_TYPE = 'PHISHING_SCREENSHOT'
LIMIT 3;

-- 6. One fraud case file, summarised into a decision draft from every source
SELECT f.CASE_ID, f.DECISION, c.AGE, c.VULNERABLE_FLAG,
       AI_COMPLETE('claude-sonnet-4-5', CONCAT(
           'You are a fraud operations team leader. Draft a 150-word case summary and a reimbursement recommendation, ',
           'citing the evidence, and flag anything in the sources that disagrees. Case notes: ', f.INVESTIGATOR_NOTES,
           ' Customer call: ', COALESCE(t.TRANSCRIPT, 'none'),
           ' Customer age: ', c.AGE, '. On the vulnerable customers register: ', IFF(c.VULNERABLE_FLAG, 'yes', 'no'),
           '. Decision recorded: ', f.DECISION)) AS DECISION_DRAFT
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_FRAUD_CASES f
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_CUSTOMERS c ON c.CUSTOMER_ID = f.CUSTOMER_ID
LEFT JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_CALL_TRANSCRIPTS t
       ON t.CUSTOMER_ID = f.CUSTOMER_ID AND t.QUEUE = 'FRAUD' AND t.TXN_ID = f.FIRST_FRAUD_TXN_ID
WHERE f.FRAUD_TYPE = 'APP_SCAM' AND t.CALL_ID IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY f.CASE_ID
LIMIT 1;

-- 7. SAR narrative quality check: one AI_EXTRACT question per element, scored against the planted QA_ISSUE
WITH x AS (
    SELECT SAR_ID, QA_ISSUE,
           AI_EXTRACT(text => NARRATIVE, responseFormat => {
               'reason': 'Why does the bank consider this activity suspicious? Answer None if no reason is given.',
               'date':   'What is the specific date of the activity? Answer None if no date is given.',
               'amount': 'What specific amount of money in pounds is mentioned? Answer None if none.',
               'action': 'What action did the bank take or will it take? Answer None if no action is stated.'}):response AS R
    FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_SAR_NARRATIVES
), f AS (
    SELECT SAR_ID, QA_ISSUE,
           CASE WHEN COALESCE(R:date::STRING, 'none') ILIKE 'none%' OR COALESCE(R:amount::STRING, 'none') ILIKE 'none%' THEN 'MISSING_DATES_AMOUNTS'
                WHEN COALESCE(R:action::STRING, 'none') ILIKE 'none%' THEN 'MISSING_ACTION'
                WHEN COALESCE(R:reason::STRING, 'none') ILIKE 'none%' THEN 'MISSING_REASON'
                ELSE 'COMPLETE' END AS AI_FINDING
    FROM x
)
SELECT QA_ISSUE, AI_FINDING, COUNT(*) AS SARS,
       ROUND(100 * SUM(COUNT_IF(QA_ISSUE = AI_FINDING)) OVER () / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER ()) AS PCT_MATCH
FROM f GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 3 DESC;

**Tip:** Search narrows 20,000 customers to 10 candidates per name; the date of birth and town then decide. Name similarity alone matches many people who just share a common name.

2. Decide: score each candidate: 50 points if the date of birth matches (also try day and month swapped), 20 if the town matches, plus 0.3 times JAROWINKLER_SIMILARITY of the names (turn "SURNAME, First" round first). Keep the best candidate: MATCH at 75 or more, REVIEW from 45, otherwise NO_MATCH.
Then check it against the answer key: TRUE_CUSTOMER_ID is the real customer (NULL for people who aren't customers) and VARIATION says how the name was changed. Answer one question both ways, "customers worried about savings rates who might leave": first with RB_CALL_SEARCH, then with AI_CLASSIFY or the RB_CALL_INSIGHTS labels plus AI_AGG over those calls. Show both results side by side, then explain when a search service is the right tool, when AI SQL is enough, and how an agent would use RB_CALL_SEARCH as a tool.

modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- AI5 (OPTIONAL): CORTEX SEARCH OVER CALL TRANSCRIPTS AND CASE NOTES - reference SQL
-- Cortex Search is not yet approved at Barclays: this module shows what it would unlock.
-- Needs setup/10b_search_lab.sql. Run as HOL_PARTICIPANT.
-- =====================================================
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;
USE SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.SEARCH_LAB;

-- 1. A search service over every call transcript, with filterable attributes
CREATE OR REPLACE CORTEX SEARCH SERVICE RB_CALL_SEARCH
    ON TRANSCRIPT
    ATTRIBUTES QUEUE, TOPIC, CHURNED
    WAREHOUSE = BARCLAYS_WH
    TARGET_LAG = '1 day'
    COMMENT = 'AI5: semantic search over retail call transcripts'
AS
SELECT t.CALL_ID, t.CUSTOMER_ID, t.CALL_START_TS, t.QUEUE, t.TOPIC, IFF(c.CHURNED, 'yes', 'no') AS CHURNED, t.TRANSCRIPT
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_CALL_TRANSCRIPTS t
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_CUSTOMERS c ON c.CUSTOMER_ID = t.CUSTOMER_ID;

-- 2. Ask it in plain English, with and without a filter
SELECT PARSE_JSON(SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SEARCH_PREVIEW('BARCLAYS_HOL.SEARCH_LAB.RB_CALL_SEARCH',
    '{"query": "customer upset that their local branch is closing and they cannot use the app", "columns": ["CALL_ID", "CUSTOMER_ID", "QUEUE", "CHURNED"], "limit": 5}'))['results'] AS RESULTS;

SELECT PARSE_JSON(SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SEARCH_PREVIEW('BARCLAYS_HOL.SEARCH_LAB.RB_CALL_SEARCH',
    '{"query": "caller told to move money to a safe account", "columns": ["CALL_ID", "CUSTOMER_ID", "TOPIC"], "filter": {"@eq": {"QUEUE": "FRAUD"}}, "limit": 5}'))['results'] AS RESULTS;

-- 3. A second service over the financial crime narratives (case notes and SARs together)
CREATE OR REPLACE CORTEX SEARCH SERVICE RB_FINCRIME_SEARCH
    ON BODY
    ATTRIBUTES DOC_TYPE, FRAUD_TYPE
    WAREHOUSE = BARCLAYS_WH
    TARGET_LAG = '1 day'
    COMMENT = 'AI5: semantic search over fraud case notes and SAR narratives'
AS
SELECT CASE_ID AS DOC_ID, 'FRAUD_CASE' AS DOC_TYPE, FRAUD_TYPE, CUSTOMER_ID, INVESTIGATOR_NOTES AS BODY FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_FRAUD_CASES
UNION ALL
SELECT SAR_ID, 'SAR', NULL, CUSTOMER_ID, NARRATIVE FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_SAR_NARRATIVES;

SELECT PARSE_JSON(SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SEARCH_PREVIEW('BARCLAYS_HOL.SEARCH_LAB.RB_FINCRIME_SEARCH',
    '{"query": "money mule receiving funds and moving them on within minutes", "columns": ["DOC_ID", "DOC_TYPE", "CUSTOMER_ID"], "limit": 5}'))['results'] AS RESULTS;

-- 4. Fuzzy name matching: a search service over customer names
CREATE OR REPLACE CORTEX SEARCH SERVICE RB_CUSTOMER_NAME_SEARCH
    ON FULL_NAME
    ATTRIBUTES CITY
    WAREHOUSE = BARCLAYS_WH
    TARGET_LAG = '1 day'
    COMMENT = 'AI5: fuzzy search over customer names'
AS
SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, FIRST_NAME || ' ' || LAST_NAME AS FULL_NAME, CITY, TO_VARCHAR(DATE_OF_BIRTH, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS DOB
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_CUSTOMERS;

SELECT * FROM TABLE(CORTEX_SEARCH_RETRIEVE(service_name => 'BARCLAYS_HOL.SEARCH_LAB.RB_CUSTOMER_NAME_SEARCH', query => 'Liz Moor', limit => 5));

-- 5. Match every outside name: search for 10 candidates, then decide on date of birth, town and name similarity
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE RB_NAME_MATCHES AS
WITH cand AS (
    SELECT m.MENTION_ID, r.CUSTOMER_ID,
           (r.DOB::DATE = TRY_TO_DATE(m.DOB_AS_WRITTEN, 'DD/MM/YYYY') OR r.DOB::DATE = TRY_TO_DATE(m.DOB_AS_WRITTEN, 'MM/DD/YYYY')) AS DOB_MATCH,
           UPPER(r.CITY) = UPPER(m.TOWN) AS TOWN_MATCH,
           JAROWINKLER_SIMILARITY(UPPER(r.FULL_NAME), UPPER(REGEXP_REPLACE(m.NAME_AS_WRITTEN, '^([^,]+), (.+)$', '\\2 \\1'))) AS NAME_SIM
    FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_NAME_MENTIONS m,
    LATERAL CORTEX_SEARCH_RETRIEVE(service_name => 'BARCLAYS_HOL.SEARCH_LAB.RB_CUSTOMER_NAME_SEARCH', query => m.NAME_AS_WRITTEN, limit => 10) r
), best AS (
    SELECT *, 50 * COALESCE(DOB_MATCH::INT, 0) + 20 * COALESCE(TOWN_MATCH::INT, 0) + 0.3 * NAME_SIM AS SCORE
    FROM cand QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY MENTION_ID ORDER BY SCORE DESC) = 1
)
SELECT m.MENTION_ID, m.SOURCE, m.NAME_AS_WRITTEN, m.DOB_AS_WRITTEN, m.TOWN, b.CUSTOMER_ID AS MATCHED_CUSTOMER_ID,
       b.DOB_MATCH, b.TOWN_MATCH, b.NAME_SIM, b.SCORE,
       CASE WHEN b.SCORE >= 75 THEN 'MATCH' WHEN b.SCORE >= 45 THEN 'REVIEW' ELSE 'NO_MATCH' END AS DECISION,
       m.TRUE_CUSTOMER_ID, m.VARIATION
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_NAME_MENTIONS m LEFT JOIN best b USING (MENTION_ID);

-- Score it against the answer key
SELECT VARIATION, COUNT(*) AS MENTIONS,
       COUNT_IF(DECISION = 'MATCH' AND MATCHED_CUSTOMER_ID = TRUE_CUSTOMER_ID) AS RIGHT_MATCH,
       COUNT_IF(DECISION = 'MATCH' AND MATCHED_CUSTOMER_ID IS DISTINCT FROM TRUE_CUSTOMER_ID) AS WRONG_MATCH,
       COUNT_IF(DECISION = 'REVIEW') AS REVIEW, COUNT_IF(DECISION = 'NO_MATCH') AS NO_MATCH
FROM RB_NAME_MATCHES GROUP BY ROLLUP (VARIATION) ORDER BY VARIATION NULLS LAST;

-- For comparison: name similarity alone, across every customer
WITH m AS (SELECT MENTION_ID, TRUE_CUSTOMER_ID, UPPER(REGEXP_REPLACE(NAME_AS_WRITTEN, '^([^,]+), (.+)$', '\\2 \\1')) AS Q FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_NAME_MENTIONS),
b AS (SELECT m.*, c.CUSTOMER_ID, JAROWINKLER_SIMILARITY(UPPER(c.FIRST_NAME || ' ' || c.LAST_NAME), m.Q) AS SIM
      FROM m JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RB_CUSTOMERS c ON TRUE QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY MENTION_ID ORDER BY SIM DESC) = 1)
SELECT COUNT_IF(SIM >= 90 AND CUSTOMER_ID = TRUE_CUSTOMER_ID) AS RIGHT_MATCH,
       COUNT_IF(SIM >= 90 AND CUSTOMER_ID IS DISTINCT FROM TRUE_CUSTOMER_ID) AS WRONG_MATCH
FROM b;

SHOW CORTEX SEARCH SERVICES IN SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.SEARCH_LAB;

modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE GOV2: LINEAGE, AUDIT AND TRUST   (~30 min)
-- Persona: Governance / Risk / Audit
-- Question: "If a source Iceberg table changes, what breaks? And who - human
--            or AI agent - has been reading client data?"
-- Prereq:   C1 only. Uses the ready-made audit pack in BARCLAYS_HOL.AUDIT_PACK
--           (setup/06_audit_pack.sql); ask PAYMENTS_AUDIT_AGENT a few questions first.
-- Note:     ACCOUNT_USAGE views have up to ~3 hours latency. Run the
--           immediate checks first; revisit the history queries at the end of the day.
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;
USE SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.AUDIT_PACK;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- GOV2.1 Impact analysis: what depends on the PAYMENTS Iceberg table? (immediate)
-- Snowsight: Catalog > BARCLAYS_HOL > RAW_DATA > PAYMENTS > Lineage tab
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT DISTANCE, TARGET_OBJECT_DOMAIN, TARGET_OBJECT_DATABASE || '.' || TARGET_OBJECT_SCHEMA || '.' || TARGET_OBJECT_NAME AS DOWNSTREAM_OBJECT
FROM TABLE(SNOWFLAKE.CORE.GET_LINEAGE('BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS', 'TABLE', 'DOWNSTREAM', 3))
ORDER BY DISTANCE, DOWNSTREAM_OBJECT;

-- And upstream: where do the agent's answers come from?
SELECT DISTANCE, SOURCE_OBJECT_DOMAIN, SOURCE_OBJECT_DATABASE || '.' || SOURCE_OBJECT_SCHEMA || '.' || SOURCE_OBJECT_NAME AS UPSTREAM_OBJECT
FROM TABLE(SNOWFLAKE.CORE.GET_LINEAGE('BARCLAYS_HOL.AUDIT_PACK.PAYMENTS_AUDIT_AGENT', 'CORTEX_AGENT', 'UPSTREAM', 3))
ORDER BY DISTANCE, UPSTREAM_OBJECT;
-- A row shown as ***.***.*** is an object in the lineage that your role has no
-- privileges on (here the platform team's SEED schema). Lineage never leaks
-- the existence of objects you are not entitled to see.

-- Object dependencies (views, dynamic tables, semantic views) - immediate
SELECT REFERENCING_OBJECT_NAME, REFERENCING_OBJECT_DOMAIN, REFERENCED_OBJECT_NAME
FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES
WHERE REFERENCED_DATABASE = 'BARCLAYS_HOL'
ORDER BY REFERENCED_OBJECT_NAME
LIMIT 50;

-- Make sure there is a restricted-column read to find
SELECT * FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.AUDIT_PACK.CLIENT_ACCOUNTS LIMIT 5;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- GOV2.2 Who accessed restricted columns? (ACCOUNT_USAGE latency applies)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT ah.QUERY_START_TIME, ah.USER_NAME,
       obj.value:objectName::STRING     AS OBJECT_NAME,
       col.value:columnName::STRING     AS COLUMN_NAME
FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.ACCESS_HISTORY ah,
     LATERAL FLATTEN(ah.BASE_OBJECTS_ACCESSED) obj,
     LATERAL FLATTEN(obj.value:columns) col
WHERE obj.value:objectName::STRING ILIKE 'BARCLAYS_HOL.%'
  AND col.value:columnName::STRING IN ('IBAN', 'ACCOUNT_NUMBER', 'SORT_CODE')
  AND ah.QUERY_START_TIME >= DATEADD('day', -1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
ORDER BY ah.QUERY_START_TIME DESC
LIMIT 20;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- GOV2.3 What are our agents doing? Every agent call is observable
-- Snowsight: AI & ML > Agents > PAYMENTS_AUDIT_AGENT > Monitoring
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT QUERY_TYPE, USER_NAME, ROLE_NAME, START_TIME, TOTAL_ELAPSED_TIME / 1000 AS SECONDS,
       LEFT(QUERY_TEXT, 120) AS QUERY_PREVIEW
FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY
WHERE DATABASE_NAME = 'BARCLAYS_HOL'
  AND QUERY_TEXT ILIKE '%SEMANTIC_VIEW%'
  AND START_TIME >= DATEADD('day', -1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
ORDER BY START_TIME DESC
LIMIT 20;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- GOV2.4 Document the data product so humans and AI find the right thing
-- -----------------------------------------------------
COMMENT ON TABLE PAYMENT_SLA_DAILY IS
  'Daily SLA compliance per payment scheme. Owner: Payments Operations. Grain: day x scheme. Source: Iceberg RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS and RAW_DATA.SLA_DEFINITIONS.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN PAYMENT_SLA_DAILY.SLA_STATUS IS
  'COMPLIANT = met success-rate and P95 targets; AT RISK = within 5% of success target; BREACH = otherwise';

-- Ask CoCo:
--   "If I drop column PROCESSING_TIME_MS from BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS,
--    which downstream objects and agents break? Use lineage to check."
--   "Produce a one-page data product card for PAYMENT_SLA_DAILY: owner, grain,
--    lineage, quality checks, sensitivity tags and consumers."

-- Barclayflake note: Trust Center and Horizon Catalog surface the same lineage,
-- classification and access history centrally for the CDO / data office.

SELECT 'GOV2 complete' AS STATUS;

steps.body:
1. Open `notebooks/` > **gov3_ai_gateway.ipynb** in the file explorer.
2. In the notebook toolbar, click the arrow next to the status dot (right of the blue run button).
3. Choose **Create new service**.
- Already created one in another module? Pick it under **Select service** instead, usually `USER_SERVICE_1`.
4. Expand **Service settings** and fill in **Connect your notebook** as below. Only the three **bold** rows change.
| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Service name | leave the default (e.g. `USER_SERVICE_1`) |
| Artifact repositories | leave as is (`SNOWFLAKE.SNOWPARK.PYPI_SHARED_REPOSITORY`) |
| Enable distributed compute | off |
| Runtime | leave as is (v3.0 · Python 3.12) |
| Compute type | CPU |
| Custom image | leave empty |
| **Compute pool** | **NOTEBOOK_POOL** (change it from HOL_COMPUTE_POOL_CPU) |
| **Idle timeout** | **1 hour** (change it from 24 hours) |
| **External access integrations** | **HOL_NOTEBOOK_ACCESS_INTEGRATION** (lets notebooks reach Postgres and the AI Gateway; set it here so one service works for every notebook module) |
| Secrets | leave empty |
5. Click **Create and connect**. The first start takes 1-2 minutes.
6. Check the role is **HOL_PARTICIPANT** and the warehouse is **BARCLAYS_WH**, using the role and warehouse button in the notebook toolbar.
**Important:** if you can't see `notebooks/` and `vignettes/`, you're in the wrong Workspace. Pick **payments-hol** from the Workspace dropdown (top left).
The starter notebook has one numbered heading per step, so Cortex Code puts each cell in the right place.
A notebook runs on its own **notebook service**, which you create once with these settings.
steps.where: the **payments-hol** Workspace (not My Workspace) > file explorer > `notebooks/gov3_ai_gateway.ipynb`
steps.expect: the starter notebook open in payments-hol with its numbered headings, and the status dot showing the service connected
steps.mediaCaption: Open the notebook > Create new service > NOTEBOOK_POOL, 1 hour, HOL_NOTEBOOK_ACCESS_INTEGRATION

steps.title: Inspect the gateway
steps.where: the Cortex Code sidebar, with `gov3_ai_gateway` open
steps.prompt: In the open notebook gov3_ai_gateway, put each cell I ask for under its matching numbered heading. Under heading 1, add a SQL cell named gateway that runs SHOW AI GATEWAYS and a SQL cell named gateway_spec that runs DESCRIBE AI GATEWAY SNOWFLAKE. Run them and explain the specification: which models it exposes, whether logging is on, and whether prompts and responses are captured.
steps.expect: one gateway, `SNOWFLAKE`, with its base URL. The specification exposes every model (`name: '*'`) and logs every request's metadata; prompts and responses are **not** captured unless an administrator turns payload capture on.

steps.title: Give yourself a short-lived key
steps.prompt: Add a Python cell named make_key that generates an RSA key pair in memory with the cryptography package and registers the public key on my own user with ALTER USER ADD KEY PAIR GOV3_GATEWAY_KEY PUBLIC_KEY = '<base64 DER public key>' ROLE_RESTRICTION = 'HOL_PARTICIPANT' DAYS_TO_EXPIRY = 1, using get_active_session(). Remove any existing GOV3_GATEWAY_KEY first (REMOVE KEY PAIR has no IF EXISTS, so wrap it in try/except). Keep the private key in a variable called key; never print or save it. Then run SHOW USER KEY PAIRS. Use vignettes/gov3_ai_gateway/gov3_gateway_calls.py in the Workspace as the reference.
steps.expect: `GOV3_GATEWAY_KEY` listed with role restriction `HOL_PARTICIPANT` and an expiry tomorrow. The gateway accepts the same tokens as other Snowflake REST APIs: OAuth, a key-pair JWT or a programmatic access token. A key that's tied to one role and expires in a day can only do what the lab role can, and only today.

steps.title: Call two model families through the gateway
steps.prompt: Add a Python cell named gateway_calls that builds a key-pair JWT from key (issuer ACCOUNT.USER.SHA256:<public key fingerprint>, subject ACCOUNT.USER, 50 minute expiry, signed RS256 with cryptography) and calls the gateway at https://<org>-<account>.snowflakecomputing.com/api/v2/aigateways/snowflake, with underscores in the host replaced by hyphens. Send the header X-Snowflake-Authorization-Token-Type: KEYPAIR_JWT and the conversation header x-snowflake-ai-gateway-conversation-id: gov3-lab. Make two calls with urllib: openai-gpt-5 on /v1/chat/completions asking "In two sentences, why might a CHAPS payment be returned, and what should the operations team check first?", and claude-sonnet-4-5 on /v1/messages asking the same about a delayed SEPA payment. Print each answer and its token usage. Use gov3_gateway_calls.py as the reference.
steps.expect: two answers, one from each model family, each with its token counts. Same endpoint, same credential, two API formats: the gateway routes each request to the right model. Any client that can change its base URL (a coding agent, the OpenAI SDK, an agent framework) could make these calls.

steps.title: See what the gateway recorded
steps.prompt: Add a SQL cell named my_traces over TABLE(AGENT_TRACE_TABLE('SNOWFLAKE')) for the last hour: one row per trace with the start time, user (resource_attributes:"user"), model (record_attributes:"gen_ai.request.model"), conversation id (record_attributes:"gen_ai.conversation.id"), input and output tokens (record_attributes:"gen_ai.usage.input_tokens" and "gen_ai.usage.output_tokens"), duration in milliseconds, and status (http.status_code below 400 is success). Run it and explain the difference between a conversation, a trace and a span.
steps.expect: your two calls, tagged with your user, the model, the `gov3-lab` conversation and their tokens and duration. You see only your own traces: a role with **MONITOR** on the gateway sees everyone's. The same data is charted in Snowsight under **AI & ML > AI Gateway > Observability**.

steps.title: Draft a tighter model policy
steps.prompt: Add a markdown cell explaining the gateway specification, then a code cell (don't run it) with the ALTER AI GATEWAY SNOWFLAKE FROM SPECIFICATION statement an account administrator would run to expose only claude-sonnet-4-5, claude-haiku-4-5 and openai-gpt-5, keep logging on, turn on prompt and response capture, and exclude users tagged BARCLAYS_HOL.GOVERNANCE.PAYLOAD_CAPTURE_EXEMPT from capture. Explain why FROM SPECIFICATION replaces the whole specification, why captured prompts make the trace table sensitive, and how CORTEX_MODELS_ALLOWLIST differs from the gateway's model list.
steps.expect: a reviewed specification change, not applied: attendees aren't account administrators, which is the point. The gateway list controls what this door exposes; `CORTEX_MODELS_ALLOWLIST` controls which models anyone in the account can use at all. Capturing prompts helps audit and evaluation but puts customer data into the trace table, so restrict who can read it, and exempt sensitive users.

steps.title: See who is using which model
steps.prompt: Add a SQL cell named usage_by_model over TABLE(AGENT_TRACE_TABLE('SNOWFLAKE')) for the last day: requests, input tokens and output tokens per user and model, plus the failure count. Then add a markdown cell explaining where an AI governance lead gets authoritative credits (SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.AI_GATEWAY_USAGE_HISTORY, which lags), and the controls they can apply: budgets, per-user quotas, and revoking USAGE on the gateway from a role.
steps.expect: your usage by model. Traces show what happened per request; credits come from `AI_GATEWAY_USAGE_HISTORY`, and per-user quotas or a budget stop spend before it surprises you.

modules.check: `gov3_traces` passes once the gateway has recorded at least two of your requests today. Remove your key when you're done: `ALTER USER REMOVE KEY PAIR GOV3_GATEWAY_KEY` (it expires tomorrow anyway).
modules.note: One endpoint, one identity, one trace table for every AI client means the AI governance lead can answer "who used which model, on what, at what cost" from Snowflake alone, and change the policy in one place.
modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- GOV3: AI governance with Cortex AI Gateway - reference SQL
-- The calls themselves are Python (gov3_gateway_calls.py); this is the SQL around them.
-- =====================================================
USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;

-- 1. The gateway Snowflake created for this account, and its specification
SHOW AI GATEWAYS;
DESCRIBE AI GATEWAY SNOWFLAKE;

-- 2. Your key pair (registered from the notebook with ALTER USER ADD KEY PAIR)
SHOW USER KEY PAIRS;

-- 3. What the gateway recorded for you in the last hour: one row per trace
WITH spans AS (
    SELECT trace:"trace_id"::STRING                                         AS TRACE_ID,
           resource_attributes:"user"::STRING                               AS USER_NAME,
           record_attributes:"gen_ai.request.model"::STRING                 AS MODEL,
           record_attributes:"gen_ai.conversation.id"::STRING               AS CONVERSATION_ID,
           TRY_TO_NUMBER(record_attributes:"gen_ai.usage.input_tokens"::STRING)  AS INPUT_TOKENS,
           TRY_TO_NUMBER(record_attributes:"gen_ai.usage.output_tokens"::STRING) AS OUTPUT_TOKENS,
           TRY_TO_NUMBER(record_attributes:"http.status_code"::STRING)      AS HTTP_STATUS,
           start_timestamp, timestamp
    FROM TABLE(AGENT_TRACE_TABLE('SNOWFLAKE'))
    WHERE timestamp >= DATEADD('hour', -1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
)
SELECT TRACE_ID, MIN(start_timestamp) AS STARTED_AT, MAX(USER_NAME) AS USER_NAME, MAX(MODEL) AS MODEL,
       MAX(CONVERSATION_ID) AS CONVERSATION_ID, SUM(INPUT_TOKENS) AS INPUT_TOKENS, SUM(OUTPUT_TOKENS) AS OUTPUT_TOKENS,
       DATEDIFF('millisecond', MIN(start_timestamp), MAX(timestamp)) AS DURATION_MS,
       IFF(COUNT_IF(HTTP_STATUS >= 400) = 0, 'SUCCESS', 'FAILURE') AS STATUS
FROM spans
GROUP BY TRACE_ID
ORDER BY STARTED_AT DESC;

-- 4. Draft only: a tighter specification. Needs ACCOUNTADMIN, and FROM SPECIFICATION
--    replaces the whole specification, so start from what DESCRIBE returns.
-- CREATE TAG IF NOT EXISTS BARCLAYS_HOL.GOVERNANCE.PAYLOAD_CAPTURE_EXEMPT;
-- ALTER AI GATEWAY SNOWFLAKE FROM SPECIFICATION $$
-- schema_version: 1
-- models:
--   - name: claude-sonnet-4-5
--   - name: claude-haiku-4-5
--   - name: openai-gpt-5
-- logging:
--   enabled: true
--   capture_payload:
--     request_response: true
--     exclude_tags:
--       - BARCLAYS_HOL.GOVERNANCE.PAYLOAD_CAPTURE_EXEMPT
-- $$;

-- 5. Usage per user and model in the last day (your own rows unless you have MONITOR)
SELECT resource_attributes:"user"::STRING                                       AS USER_NAME,
       record_attributes:"gen_ai.request.model"::STRING                         AS MODEL,
       COUNT(*)                                                                 AS REQUESTS,
       SUM(TRY_TO_NUMBER(record_attributes:"gen_ai.usage.input_tokens"::STRING))  AS INPUT_TOKENS,
       SUM(TRY_TO_NUMBER(record_attributes:"gen_ai.usage.output_tokens"::STRING)) AS OUTPUT_TOKENS,
       COUNT_IF(TRY_TO_NUMBER(record_attributes:"http.status_code"::STRING) >= 400) AS FAILURES
FROM TABLE(AGENT_TRACE_TABLE('SNOWFLAKE'))
WHERE timestamp >= DATEADD('day', -1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
  AND record_attributes:"gen_ai.operation.name"::STRING = 'chat'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY REQUESTS DESC;

-- Authoritative credits (lags; needs Account Usage access):
-- SELECT * FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.AI_GATEWAY_USAGE_HISTORY ORDER BY START_TIME DESC LIMIT 50;

-- 6. Clean up
-- ALTER USER REMOVE KEY PAIR GOV3_GATEWAY_KEY;

-- =====================================================
-- BARCLAYS PAYMENTS HOL v2 - CATCH-UP SCRIPT
-- CORE ANALYTICS LAYER (pure SQL equivalent of the dbt project + AI enrichment)
--
-- Run this if your chosen vignette needs the analytics layer and you have
-- not completed DE1 (dbt) / DA2 (AI enrichment). Safe to re-run.
-- Objects match dbt/models exactly so later vignettes behave the same.
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;
USE SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS;

-- ---------- Staging views ----------
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW STG_PAYMENTS AS
SELECT
    PAYMENT_ID,
    PAYMENT_DATE::TIMESTAMP                             AS PAYMENT_DATE,
    DATE_TRUNC('DAY', PAYMENT_DATE::TIMESTAMP)          AS PAYMENT_DAY,
    ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID,
    BENEFICIARY_ACCOUNT_ID,
    UPPER(TRIM(PAYMENT_TYPE))                           AS PAYMENT_TYPE,
    UPPER(TRIM(CHANNEL))                                AS CHANNEL,
    UPPER(TRIM(CURRENCY))                               AS CURRENCY,
    AMOUNT::NUMBER(15,2)                                AS AMOUNT,
    FX_RATE,
    UPPER(TRIM(STATUS))                                 AS STATUS,
    PROCESSING_TIME_MS::NUMBER                          AS PROCESSING_TIME_MS,
    ERROR_CODE,
    UPPER(TRIM(REGION))                                 AS REGION,
    SETTLEMENT_DATE,
    CASE WHEN STATUS = 'COMPLETED' THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END  AS IS_SUCCESSFUL,
    CASE WHEN STATUS = 'FAILED'    THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END  AS IS_FAILED,
    CASE WHEN ERROR_CODE IS NOT NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS HAS_ERROR
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW STG_FEEDBACK AS
SELECT
    FEEDBACK_ID,
    FEEDBACK_DATE::TIMESTAMP            AS FEEDBACK_DATE,
    DATE_TRUNC('DAY', FEEDBACK_DATE)    AS FEEDBACK_DAY,
    CUSTOMER_ID,
    PAYMENT_ID,
    UPPER(TRIM(FEEDBACK_CHANNEL))       AS FEEDBACK_CHANNEL,
    TRIM(FEEDBACK_TEXT)                 AS FEEDBACK_TEXT,
    UPPER(TRIM(PAYMENT_TYPE))           AS PAYMENT_TYPE,
    RATING::NUMBER(1)                   AS RATING,
    LENGTH(TRIM(FEEDBACK_TEXT))         AS FEEDBACK_LENGTH,
    CASE WHEN RATING >= 4 THEN 'SATISFIED'
         WHEN RATING = 3  THEN 'NEUTRAL'
         ELSE 'DISSATISFIED' END        AS SATISFACTION_TIER
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.CUSTOMER_FEEDBACK
WHERE FEEDBACK_TEXT IS NOT NULL AND LENGTH(TRIM(FEEDBACK_TEXT)) > 0;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW STG_CUSTOMERS AS
SELECT
    c.CUSTOMER_ID,
    UPPER(TRIM(c.CUSTOMER_NAME))        AS CUSTOMER_NAME,
    UPPER(TRIM(c.SECTOR))               AS SECTOR,
    c.COUNTRY,
    c.ONBOARDING_DATE,
    UPPER(TRIM(c.KYC_STATUS))           AS KYC_STATUS,
    c.RM_ID,
    r.RM_NAME,
    r.TEAM                              AS RM_TEAM,
    r.REGION                            AS RM_REGION
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.CUSTOMERS c
LEFT JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.RELATIONSHIP_MANAGERS r ON c.RM_ID = r.RM_ID;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW STG_ACCOUNTS AS
SELECT
    a.ACCOUNT_ID, a.CUSTOMER_ID, a.SORT_CODE, a.ACCOUNT_NUMBER, a.IBAN, a.BIC,
    UPPER(TRIM(a.CURRENCY))             AS CURRENCY,
    UPPER(TRIM(a.ACCOUNT_TYPE))         AS ACCOUNT_TYPE,
    UPPER(TRIM(a.STATUS))               AS STATUS,
    a.OPENED_DATE,
    c.CUSTOMER_NAME,
    c.SECTOR                            AS CUSTOMER_SECTOR
FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.ACCOUNTS a
LEFT JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.CUSTOMERS c ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID;

-- ---------- Marts ----------
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE MART_PAYMENT_KPIS AS
SELECT
    p.PAYMENT_DAY, p.PAYMENT_TYPE, p.REGION, p.CHANNEL,
    c.SECTOR AS CUSTOMER_SECTOR, c.RM_NAME, c.RM_TEAM,
    COUNT(*)                                                   AS TOTAL_PAYMENTS,
    SUM(p.AMOUNT)                                              AS TOTAL_VOLUME_GBP,
    ROUND(AVG(p.AMOUNT), 2)                                    AS AVG_PAYMENT_AMOUNT,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN p.IS_SUCCESSFUL THEN 1 END)                AS SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN p.IS_FAILED     THEN 1 END)                AS FAILED_PAYMENTS,
    ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN p.IS_SUCCESSFUL THEN 1 END)::FLOAT / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) * 100, 2) AS SUCCESS_RATE_PCT,
    ROUND(AVG(p.PROCESSING_TIME_MS), 0)                        AS AVG_PROCESSING_TIME_MS,
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY p.PROCESSING_TIME_MS), 0) AS P95_PROCESSING_TIME_MS
FROM STG_PAYMENTS p
LEFT JOIN STG_ACCOUNTS  a ON p.ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID
LEFT JOIN STG_CUSTOMERS c ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
GROUP BY p.PAYMENT_DAY, p.PAYMENT_TYPE, p.REGION, p.CHANNEL, c.SECTOR, c.RM_NAME, c.RM_TEAM;

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE MART_SLA_COMPLIANCE AS
WITH daily_scheme AS (
    SELECT PAYMENT_DAY, PAYMENT_TYPE,
           SUM(TOTAL_PAYMENTS) AS TOTAL_PAYMENTS,
           SUM(SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS) AS SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS,
           SUM(FAILED_PAYMENTS) AS FAILED_PAYMENTS,
           ROUND(SUM(SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS)::FLOAT / NULLIF(SUM(TOTAL_PAYMENTS), 0) * 100, 2) AS SUCCESS_RATE_PCT,
           MAX(P95_PROCESSING_TIME_MS) AS P95_PROCESSING_TIME_MS
    FROM MART_PAYMENT_KPIS
    GROUP BY PAYMENT_DAY, PAYMENT_TYPE
)
SELECT
    d.PAYMENT_DAY, d.PAYMENT_TYPE, s.SLA_NAME,
    s.TARGET_SUCCESS_RATE    AS SLA_TARGET_PCT,
    s.MAX_PROCESSING_TIME_MS AS SLA_THRESHOLD_MS,
    d.SUCCESS_RATE_PCT       AS ACTUAL_SUCCESS_RATE,
    d.P95_PROCESSING_TIME_MS AS ACTUAL_P95_MS,
    d.TOTAL_PAYMENTS, d.FAILED_PAYMENTS,
    CASE WHEN d.SUCCESS_RATE_PCT >= s.TARGET_SUCCESS_RATE
           AND d.P95_PROCESSING_TIME_MS <= s.MAX_PROCESSING_TIME_MS THEN 'COMPLIANT'
         WHEN d.SUCCESS_RATE_PCT >= s.TARGET_SUCCESS_RATE * 0.95 THEN 'AT RISK'
         ELSE 'BREACH' END   AS SLA_STATUS,
    ROUND(d.SUCCESS_RATE_PCT - s.TARGET_SUCCESS_RATE, 2) AS RATE_GAP_PCT,
    d.P95_PROCESSING_TIME_MS - s.MAX_PROCESSING_TIME_MS  AS TIME_GAP_MS
FROM daily_scheme d
JOIN BARCLAYS_HOL.RAW_DATA.SLA_DEFINITIONS s ON d.PAYMENT_TYPE = s.PAYMENT_TYPE;

-- CoCo-built marts from the original lab (DE1 step 3), pre-built here
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE MART_CUSTOMER_PAYMENTS AS
WITH base AS (
    SELECT c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.CUSTOMER_NAME, c.SECTOR AS CUSTOMER_SECTOR, c.RM_NAME,
           p.PAYMENT_TYPE, p.AMOUNT, p.IS_SUCCESSFUL, p.PROCESSING_TIME_MS
    FROM STG_PAYMENTS p
    JOIN STG_ACCOUNTS  a ON p.ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID
    JOIN STG_CUSTOMERS c ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
), top_scheme AS (
    SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, PAYMENT_TYPE AS MOST_USED_SCHEME
    FROM base GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID, PAYMENT_TYPE
    QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CUSTOMER_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) = 1
)
SELECT b.CUSTOMER_ID, b.CUSTOMER_NAME, b.CUSTOMER_SECTOR, b.RM_NAME,
       COUNT(*)                                                   AS TOTAL_PAYMENTS,
       SUM(b.AMOUNT)                                              AS TOTAL_VOLUME_GBP,
       ROUND(COUNT_IF(b.IS_SUCCESSFUL)::FLOAT / COUNT(*) * 100, 2) AS SUCCESS_RATE_PCT,
       ROUND(AVG(b.PROCESSING_TIME_MS), 0)                        AS AVG_PROCESSING_TIME_MS,
       t.MOST_USED_SCHEME
FROM base b JOIN top_scheme t USING (CUSTOMER_ID)
GROUP BY b.CUSTOMER_ID, b.CUSTOMER_NAME, b.CUSTOMER_SECTOR, b.RM_NAME, t.MOST_USED_SCHEME;

-- ---------- AI enrichment (DA2 builds this step by step) ----------
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE FEEDBACK_ENRICHED AS
WITH ai_scored AS (
    SELECT f.*, c.CUSTOMER_NAME, c.SECTOR AS CUSTOMER_SECTOR, c.RM_NAME,
           -- AI_SENTIMENT returns a label, so map the overall label to -1, 0 or 1
           -- (legacy SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SENTIMENT is blocked on new accounts)
           DECODE(GET(FILTER(AI_SENTIMENT(f.FEEDBACK_TEXT):categories, c -> c:name::STRING = 'overall'), 0):sentiment::STRING,
                  'positive', 1, 'negative', -1, 0)::FLOAT AS SENTIMENT_SCORE,
           AI_CLASSIFY(f.FEEDBACK_TEXT,
               ['Performance Issue','Service Quality','Technical Problem',
                'Positive Experience','Feature Request']) AS CLASSIFICATION_RESULT
    FROM STG_FEEDBACK f
    LEFT JOIN STG_CUSTOMERS c ON f.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
)
SELECT FEEDBACK_ID, FEEDBACK_DATE, CUSTOMER_ID, CUSTOMER_NAME, CUSTOMER_SECTOR, RM_NAME,
       PAYMENT_ID, FEEDBACK_CHANNEL, FEEDBACK_TEXT, PAYMENT_TYPE, RATING, SENTIMENT_SCORE,
       CASE WHEN SENTIMENT_SCORE >  0.3 THEN 'POSITIVE'
            WHEN SENTIMENT_SCORE < -0.3 THEN 'NEGATIVE'
            ELSE 'NEUTRAL' END                      AS SENTIMENT_LABEL,
       CLASSIFICATION_RESULT:labels[0]::STRING      AS TOPIC_CATEGORY
FROM ai_scored;

SELECT 'Core analytics catch-up complete' AS STATUS,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM MART_PAYMENT_KPIS)   AS KPI_ROWS,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM MART_SLA_COMPLIANCE) AS SLA_ROWS,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM FEEDBACK_ENRICHED)   AS FEEDBACK_ROWS;

-- =====================================================
-- BARCLAYS PAYMENTS HOL v2 - CATCH-UP SCRIPT
-- SEMANTIC VIEW SV_PAYMENTS + PAYMENTS_ASSISTANT AGENT
-- Adapted from gemmamcginlay-sf/barclays-hol sql/05_intelligence.sql
-- Requires: setup/catchup/core_analytics.sql (or DE1 + DA2)
-- Used by: OPS1, OPS2, AI1, AI2 if you skipped DA1
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BARCLAYS_WH;
USE SCHEMA BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS;

-- =====================================================
-- 5.1: Create Semantic View
-- 3 logical tables, 1 relationship, 15 dimensions,
-- 16 facts, 7 metrics, 8 verified queries
-- =====================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE SEMANTIC VIEW SV_PAYMENTS

  -- Logical tables
  TABLES (
    payments AS BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.MART_PAYMENT_KPIS
      PRIMARY KEY (PAYMENT_DAY, PAYMENT_TYPE, REGION, CHANNEL, CUSTOMER_SECTOR, RM_NAME, RM_TEAM)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('payment data', 'transactions')
      COMMENT = 'Daily payment KPIs by scheme, region, channel, sector, and RM',

    sla AS BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.MART_SLA_COMPLIANCE
      PRIMARY KEY (PAYMENT_DAY, PAYMENT_TYPE)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('sla data', 'compliance', 'service levels')
      COMMENT = 'Daily SLA compliance per payment scheme',

    feedback AS BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.FEEDBACK_ENRICHED
      PRIMARY KEY (FEEDBACK_ID)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('customer feedback', 'sentiment', 'complaints')
      COMMENT = 'AI-enriched customer feedback with sentiment and topic classification'
  )

  -- Relationships
  RELATIONSHIPS (
    payments_sla AS payments (PAYMENT_DAY, PAYMENT_TYPE)
      REFERENCES sla (PAYMENT_DAY, PAYMENT_TYPE)
  )

  -- Facts
  FACTS (
    -- Payment facts
    payments.total_payments AS TOTAL_PAYMENTS
      COMMENT = 'Number of payments',
    payments.successful_payments AS SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS
      COMMENT = 'Payments with COMPLETED status',
    payments.failed_payments AS FAILED_PAYMENTS
      COMMENT = 'Payments with FAILED status',
    payments.total_volume_gbp AS TOTAL_VOLUME_GBP
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('volume', 'payment volume')
      COMMENT = 'Total amount in GBP',
    payments.avg_payment_amount AS AVG_PAYMENT_AMOUNT
      COMMENT = 'Average payment amount in GBP',
    payments.avg_processing_time_ms AS AVG_PROCESSING_TIME_MS
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('average latency')
      COMMENT = 'Average processing time (ms)',
    payments.p95_processing_time_ms AS P95_PROCESSING_TIME_MS
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('p95 latency', 'p95')
      COMMENT = '95th percentile processing time (ms)',

    -- SLA facts
    sla.sla_target_pct AS SLA_TARGET_PCT
      COMMENT = 'SLA target success rate',
    sla.sla_threshold_ms AS SLA_THRESHOLD_MS
      COMMENT = 'SLA max P95 (ms)',
    sla.actual_success_rate AS ACTUAL_SUCCESS_RATE
      COMMENT = 'Actual daily success rate',
    sla.actual_p95_ms AS ACTUAL_P95_MS
      COMMENT = 'Actual daily P95 (ms)',
    sla.rate_gap_pct AS RATE_GAP_PCT
      COMMENT = 'Success rate gap vs target',
    sla.time_gap_ms AS TIME_GAP_MS
      COMMENT = 'P95 gap vs threshold (ms)',

    -- Feedback facts
    feedback.rating AS RATING
      COMMENT = 'Satisfaction rating 1 to 5',
    feedback.sentiment_score AS SENTIMENT_SCORE
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('sentiment')
      COMMENT = 'AI sentiment -1.0 to +1.0'
  )

  -- Dimensions
  DIMENSIONS (
    -- Payment dimensions
    payments.payment_type AS PAYMENT_TYPE
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('scheme', 'payment scheme', 'rail')
      COMMENT = 'CHAPS, FASTER_PAYMENTS, BACS, SWIFT, SEPA, WIRE_TRANSFER',
    payments.channel AS CHANNEL
      COMMENT = 'API, Online Banking, Branch, File Upload, Mobile',
    payments.region AS REGION
      COMMENT = 'UK, EMEA, APAC, Americas',
    payments.customer_sector AS CUSTOMER_SECTOR
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('sector', 'industry')
      COMMENT = 'Industry sector of originating customer',
    payments.rm_name AS RM_NAME
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('relationship manager', 'RM', 'account manager')
      COMMENT = 'Relationship manager name',
    payments.rm_team AS RM_TEAM
      COMMENT = 'Corporate Banking, Institutional Banking, SME Banking',

    -- SLA dimensions
    sla.sla_name AS SLA_NAME
      COMMENT = 'SLA definition name',
    sla.sla_status AS SLA_STATUS
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('compliance status')
      COMMENT = 'COMPLIANT, AT RISK, or BREACH',

    -- Feedback dimensions (enables sentiment/rating breakdown by scheme, sector, RM)
    feedback.feedback_payment_type AS PAYMENT_TYPE
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('feedback scheme', 'sentiment scheme')
      COMMENT = 'Payment scheme on feedback rows: CHAPS, FASTER_PAYMENTS, BACS, SWIFT, SEPA',
    feedback.customer_name AS CUSTOMER_NAME
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('customer', 'client')
      COMMENT = 'Feedback customer',
    feedback.feedback_sector AS CUSTOMER_SECTOR
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('feedback sector')
      COMMENT = 'Sector of the customer who gave feedback',
    feedback.feedback_rm AS RM_NAME
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('feedback RM')
      COMMENT = 'RM of the customer who gave feedback',
    feedback.feedback_channel AS FEEDBACK_CHANNEL
      COMMENT = 'Email, Phone, Portal, Survey, Chat',
    feedback.sentiment_label AS SENTIMENT_LABEL
      COMMENT = 'POSITIVE, NEUTRAL, or NEGATIVE',
    feedback.topic_category AS TOPIC_CATEGORY
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('topic', 'feedback topic')
      COMMENT = 'AI-classified feedback topic'
  )

  -- Metrics (derived aggregations)
  METRICS (
    payments.success_rate AS
      ROUND(SUM(payments.successful_payments)::FLOAT
        / NULLIF(SUM(payments.total_payments), 0) * 100, 2)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('success rate', 'completion rate')
      COMMENT = 'Weighted success rate',

    payments.failure_rate AS
      ROUND(SUM(payments.failed_payments)::FLOAT
        / NULLIF(SUM(payments.total_payments), 0) * 100, 2)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('failure rate', 'error rate')
      COMMENT = 'Weighted failure rate',

    sla.breach_count AS
      COUNT(CASE WHEN sla.sla_status = 'BREACH' THEN 1 END)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('breaches', 'sla breaches')
      COMMENT = 'Number of BREACH records',

    sla.at_risk_count AS
      COUNT(CASE WHEN sla.sla_status = 'AT RISK' THEN 1 END)
      COMMENT = 'Number of AT RISK records',

    feedback.avg_sentiment AS
      ROUND(AVG(feedback.sentiment_score), 3)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('average sentiment')
      COMMENT = 'Average AI sentiment score',

    feedback.negative_feedback_count AS
      COUNT(CASE WHEN feedback.sentiment_label = 'NEGATIVE' THEN 1 END)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('complaints', 'negative reviews')
      COMMENT = 'Count of negative feedback',

    feedback.avg_rating AS
      ROUND(AVG(feedback.rating), 1)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('average rating', 'customer rating')
      COMMENT = 'Average satisfaction rating (1-5)'
  )

  COMMENT = 'Barclays Payments Operations — KPIs, SLA compliance, and customer sentiment'

  -- AI instructions
  AI_SQL_GENERATION
    'UK payments operations. Schemes: CHAPS (same-day domestic), FASTER_PAYMENTS (real-time domestic max 250K),
     BACS (T+2 domestic batch), SWIFT (T+2 international), SEPA (T+1 EUR), WIRE_TRANSFER (same-day domestic).
     SUCCESS RATE: always SUM(SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS)/SUM(TOTAL_PAYMENTS)*100, never AVG(SUCCESS_RATE_PCT).
     SLA: COMPLIANT=within thresholds, AT RISK=within 5pct of target, BREACH=below.
     VOLUME: TOTAL_VOLUME_GBP for money, TOTAL_PAYMENTS for counts.
     Processing times vary by scheme: FASTER_PAYMENTS ~500ms, SWIFT ~9000ms.
     Sentiment: -1 to +1, POSITIVE>0.3, NEGATIVE<-0.3.
     IMPORTANT: The feedback table has its own PAYMENT_TYPE, CUSTOMER_SECTOR, and RM_NAME dimensions.
     For sentiment/rating/feedback questions broken down by payment type, sector, or RM, query the
     feedback table directly using its own dimensions. Do NOT try to join to the payments table for these.'

  AI_QUESTION_CATEGORIZATION
    'Payment volumes/counts/rates/processing times/P95 -> payments table.
     SLA compliance/breaches/targets/at risk -> sla table.
     Satisfaction/sentiment/complaints/ratings/topics/feedback -> feedback table.
     Sentiment or ratings BY payment type/scheme -> feedback table (has its own PAYMENT_TYPE).
     Sentiment or ratings BY sector -> feedback table (has its own CUSTOMER_SECTOR).
     Sentiment or ratings BY RM -> feedback table (has its own RM_NAME).'

  -- Verified queries (teach the model how to answer common questions)
  AI_VERIFIED_QUERIES (
    monthly_volume AS (
      QUESTION 'What is the total payment volume this month?'
      ONBOARDING_QUESTION TRUE
      SQL 'SELECT SUM(TOTAL_VOLUME_GBP) AS total_volume_gbp
           FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.MART_PAYMENT_KPIS
           WHERE PAYMENT_DAY >= DATE_TRUNC(''MONTH'', CURRENT_DATE())'
    ),
    success_by_scheme AS (
      QUESTION 'What is the success rate by payment scheme?'
      ONBOARDING_QUESTION TRUE
      SQL 'SELECT PAYMENT_TYPE,
                  ROUND(SUM(SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS)::FLOAT / NULLIF(SUM(TOTAL_PAYMENTS), 0) * 100, 2) AS success_rate
           FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.MART_PAYMENT_KPIS
           GROUP BY PAYMENT_TYPE ORDER BY success_rate'
    ),
    sla_breaches AS (
      QUESTION 'Which schemes are breaching SLA?'
      ONBOARDING_QUESTION TRUE
      SQL 'SELECT PAYMENT_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS breach_days
           FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.MART_SLA_COMPLIANCE
           WHERE SLA_STATUS = ''BREACH''
             AND PAYMENT_DAY >= DATEADD(''day'', -30, CURRENT_DATE())
           GROUP BY PAYMENT_TYPE ORDER BY breach_days DESC'
    ),
    top_rms AS (
      QUESTION 'Top 5 relationship managers by volume?'
      SQL 'SELECT RM_NAME, SUM(TOTAL_VOLUME_GBP) AS volume
           FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.MART_PAYMENT_KPIS
           WHERE RM_NAME IS NOT NULL
           GROUP BY RM_NAME ORDER BY volume DESC LIMIT 5'
    ),
    swift_p95 AS (
      QUESTION 'Average P95 latency for SWIFT?'
      SQL 'SELECT ROUND(AVG(P95_PROCESSING_TIME_MS)) AS avg_p95_ms
           FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.MART_PAYMENT_KPIS
           WHERE PAYMENT_TYPE = ''SWIFT'''
    ),
    weekly_trend AS (
      QUESTION 'Weekly payment volume trend'
      SQL 'SELECT DATE_TRUNC(''WEEK'', PAYMENT_DAY) AS week,
                  SUM(TOTAL_PAYMENTS) AS payments
           FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.MART_PAYMENT_KPIS
           GROUP BY week ORDER BY week'
    ),
    failed_sectors AS (
      QUESTION 'Which sectors have the most failures?'
      SQL 'SELECT CUSTOMER_SECTOR, SUM(FAILED_PAYMENTS) AS failures
           FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.MART_PAYMENT_KPIS
           WHERE CUSTOMER_SECTOR IS NOT NULL
           GROUP BY CUSTOMER_SECTOR ORDER BY failures DESC'
    ),
    sentiment_schemes AS (
      QUESTION 'How does customer sentiment compare across payment types?'
      ONBOARDING_QUESTION TRUE
      SQL 'SELECT PAYMENT_TYPE, ROUND(AVG(SENTIMENT_SCORE), 3) AS avg_sentiment,
                  COUNT(*) AS feedback_count
           FROM BARCLAYS_HOL.ANALYTICS.FEEDBACK_ENRICHED
           GROUP BY PAYMENT_TYPE ORDER BY avg_sentiment'
    )
  );
